title: Vectors, Scalars and the Projectile Launch
welcome_lead: Decompose motion into perpendicular components and predict where a projectile will land.
meta_desc: A-Level Mechanics adventure on vectors, scalars and projectile motion analysis.
final_note: Mastery of components turns 2D motion into two simple 1D problems.

concepts.def: Quantity with magnitude only, no direction.
Object moving under gravity only after launch.
Total time projectile spends in the air.

walkthroughs.body_html: A velocity v at angle theta to horizontal resolves into vx = v cos(theta) and vy = v sin(theta). These act independently.
Horizontal motion is uniform (no air resistance). Vertical motion accelerates downward at g = 9.81 m/s². Use suvat on each axis.
For a projectile launched from ground level, range R = v² sin(2 theta) / g. Maximum range occurs at 45 degrees.
